title: Bank of America to Acquire 49.9% Stake in Jio Credit for $1.9 Billion
excerpt: The U.S. banking giant will become a joint venture partner in Mukesh Ambani's fast-growing NBFC arm, marking one of the largest foreign investments in India's financial services sector.
body:
• Bank of America will acquire up to 49.9% of Jio Credit, the NBFC arm of Jio Financial Services, in a deal worth ₹18,268 crore ($1.92 billion).
  • The transaction values Jio Credit at approximately $3.8 billion, initially giving BofA a 26.5% stake with potential to rise through warrant conversion.
  • Jio Credit has grown to over $3 billion in assets under management within just two years of operations, making it one of India's fastest-growing NBFCs.
  • The deal marks the latest in a wave of major foreign investments in India's financial services sector, following MUFG's investment in Shriram Finance and Emirates NBD's acquisition of RBL Bank.

The Deal Structure

Bank of America will become a joint venture partner in Jio Credit through a preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants, the two companies announced on Wednesday. Jio Credit will issue shares worth up to ₹6,613 crore and warrants worth up to ₹11,655 crore to BofA as part of the transaction.

The structure gives BofA an initial 26.5% stake in Jio Credit, with the holding potentially rising to 49.9% once all warrants are exercised. At the full investment amount, the transaction values the NBFC at around $3.8 billion, according to a Reuters calculation.

"By combining Jio Financial Services' scale, local expertise and customer base with Bank of America's global reach, digital experience and close to 250 years of leadership in banking, we can help expand access to financial services and support India's continued economic growth."

— Brian Moynihan, CEO, Bank of America

Not a Retail Banking Play

A BofA spokesperson told Reuters that the deal is not a retail banking expansion in India. Instead, the partnership focuses on Jio Credit's non-banking finance operations, which include digital lending and consumer credit products distributed through Jio's vast digital ecosystem.

Jio Credit is among India's fastest-growing NBFCs, with assets under management exceeding $3 billion as of June-end — a remarkable figure for a company that has been operational for just two years. In Q3 FY26, the NBFC's gross disbursements doubled year-on-year to ₹8,615 crore, while net interest income jumped 266% to ₹165 crore.

Jio Financial's Expanding Empire

Jio Financial Services listed in 2023 after a demerger from Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries. The company has moved aggressively into multiple financial verticals, building partnerships with some of the world's largest financial institutions.

It offers asset and wealth management services through joint ventures with BlackRock and has entered a JV with Germany's Allianz to offer general and health insurance. The Ambani-backed company also operates payment services through Jio Payments Bank, which became a wholly owned subsidiary after acquiring SBI's stake.

Foreign Capital Floods India's Financial Sector

The BofA-Jio deal is the latest in a series of major foreign investments in India's financial services industry. Japan's MUFG made a significant investment in Shriram Finance, while Dubai-based Emirates NBD acquired a 60% stake in lender RBL Bank.

India's NBFC sector has become particularly attractive to global investors as the country's credit penetration remains low compared to developed markets, offering substantial room for growth. With India's digital payments infrastructure already among the world's most advanced through UPI, the combination of digital distribution and lending represents a major opportunity.

What's Next

The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals from Indian financial regulators including the Reserve Bank of India. Given the size and strategic nature of the deal, approvals could take several months. For BofA, the partnership provides exposure to India's consumer lending boom without the complexity of setting up a full retail banking operation. For Jio Financial, BofA's capital and global expertise accelerate its push to become a dominant player in India's financial services landscape.
nri_angle: The deal positions Jio Credit as a major NBFC player backed by one of Wall Street's biggest names, creating new lending and investment options for India's growing consumer market.
